land.text: the Bahmani province around Junnar, where Malik Ahmad had been governor, and the lands the early sultans added to Daulatabad (1499)

predecessors.note: Malik Ahmad Nizam Shah I 'had been the Bahmani governor of Junnar and broke away'; Cliopatria's Bahmani row ends 1491 and Ahmadnagar's first shape is 1492.

land.text: the remnant of the Nizam Shahi state around Ahmadnagar, Junnar and Daulatabad

successors.note: Oct 1636: 'Aurangzeb defeated Shahaji and partitioned the sultanate between the Mughal Empire and the Sultanate of Bijapur.' The page gives no line between the two shares. Cliopatria assigns the whole remnant to the Mughals only from 1653 and keeps an 'Ahmadnagar' shape to 1652.

land.text: Bijapur's share of the partition (undefined on the page)

successors.note: No Cliopatria shape of Bijapur gains this land in 1636-1652; the share is unlocated.

capitals.name: Ahmednagar
capitals.note: Infobox: Ahmednagar (1494-1600); 'Ahmadnagar was founded in 1494'. Daulatabad (1499-1636) is listed as a secondary capital.

capitals.name: Paranda
capitals.note: Infobox: Paranda (1600-1610), after the Mughal capture of Ahmadnagar; Malik Ambar backed Murtaza Nizam Shah II at Paranda in 1600.

capitals.name: Junnar
capitals.note: Infobox lists Junnar again for 1610; the Malik Ambar page says he moved the capital 'from Paranda to Junnar' (undated).

capitals.name: Aurangabad (Khirki)
capitals.note: Infobox: Aurangabad (1610-1636); the Malik Ambar page: 'He founded/inhabited the city of Khirki in 1610.'

rulers.name: Bahadur Nizam Shah
rulers.note: Minor; regency of Chand Bibi (1595-1600). Last king of the Ahmadnagar line before the Mughal capture.

rulers.name: Ahmad Nizam Shah II
rulers.note: Listed for 1596 in the page's table, inside Bahadur Nizam Shah's reign.

rulers.name: Murtaza Nizam Shah II
rulers.note: Backed by Malik Ambar at Paranda in 1600; Malik Ambar 'was the regent of the Nizamshahi dynasty of Ahmednagar from 1600 to 1626' (Malik Ambar page).

rulers.name: Hussain Nizam Shah III
rulers.note: Fath Khan 'surrendered to the Mughals in the siege of Daulatabad' in 1633.

rulers.name: Murtaza Nizam Shah III
rulers.note: The Shahaji page speaks of Shahaji's 'installation of Murtaza'; the sultanate was partitioned in 1636.

correction.text: the same shape as Cliopatria's 1492-1539 row, drawn from the 28 May 1490 independence: Junnar and the Bahmani province around it

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1490-1491: the infobox gives 'Established: 28 May 1490' and 'On 28 May 1490, Ahmad declared independence'; Cliopatria starts the row in 1492. The shape is the 1492 shape unchanged. The page gives no area; it describes the sultanate at its zenith as 'extending form Khandesh to Udgir, Golna to Paranda and from Konkan to territories beyond Elichpur of Berar'.

73,856 km2 for 1492-1539, the Konkan-to-Daulatabad band around Junnar and Ahmadnagar. The page gives no area and no boundary for this span; Daulatabad was 'secured' in 1499, which the shape already includes.

Two coastal cells (about 700 km2) on the Konkan edge pass to the Portuguese in Cliopatria's 1540 row. No page opened dates or names that strip (the Ahmadnagar page mentions only Janjira, built in 1567); no event beyond the verdict, below the resolution of the pages.

75,385 km2 for 1547-1551: Cliopatria adds 12 cells in the south-east (the Solapur-Naldurg side of the Bijapur frontier) and removes one. The Adil Shahi page says Burhan Nizam Shah I 'besieged the Bijapuri city of Solapur four times, but did not retain it until a third invasion' and that Ali Adil Shah I's request for Solapur and Kaliyani was refused; no year is given, so the gain is a confidence-1 event.

73,164 km2 for 1552-1578: the same 12 cells are removed again in 1552. Whether they went back to Bijapur or are Cliopatria's revision, no page opened dates it; Kaliyani was returned in 1561 and Solapur was never returned (Adil Shahi page), so this strip is a Cliopatria artefact; kept.

correction.text: Ahmadnagar's 1552-1578 shape plus Berar from Ellichpur to Mahur, annexed in 1574

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1574-1578: 'Murtaza Shah annexed Berar in 1574, bringing the sultanate to its territorial zenith' (Ahmadnagar page; the Berar page agrees: 'annex Berar into his own dominions of the Ahmadnagar Sultanate in 1574'). Cliopatria keeps Berar as its own row to 1578 and gives the enlarged shape only from 1579.

correction.text: unchanged shape; it holds 1579-1595 only, because Berar is ceded to the Mughals in February 1596

keyframe_review.note: 152,721 km2 for 1579-1599 is the 1578 shape plus Berar, right for 1574-1595. The Chand Bibi page dates the loss of Berar to 23 February 1596 ('she decided to make peace by ceding Berar to Murad'), four years before Cliopatria gives it to the Mughals (1600); the shape holds to 1595. The Ahmadnagar infobox gives no area to compare.

correction.text: Ahmadnagar's 1579 shape without Berar (ceded to the Mughals in February 1596)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1596-1599: after 'On 23 February 1596, she decided to make peace by ceding Berar to Murad, who retreated' (Chand Bibi page) Ahmadnagar is again the pre-1574 state without Berar. Cliopatria still draws Berar inside Ahmadnagar to 1599.

56,199 km2 for 1600-1618: the Nizam Shahi remnant after 'Ahmednagar was captured by the Mughal forces of Daniyal and Mirza Yusuf Khan on 18 August 1600'. Mughal capture of Ahmadnagar fort (18 August 1600) is a loss of the town itself, but the 237-cell 'rump' still contains it: the Nizam Shahi state lived on at Paranda, Junnar and Khirki and Malik Ambar later 'captured Ahmednagar Fort and town from the Mughals' (undated on the Malik Ambar page).

correction.text: unchanged shape; it holds 1619-1636 only, because the sultanate was partitioned in October 1636

keyframe_review.note: 56,587 km2; three cells are gained from Bijapur's edge in 1619 (page silent). The shape is right to the end of the state: 'Disestablished: October 1636'. Cliopatria carries it to 1639.

correction.text: not an Ahmadnagar shape after October 1636: the remnant belongs to the Mughal Empire (and a share to Bijapur) from the partition, 1637-1647

keyframe_review.note: The sultanate no longer exists: 'In 1636 Aurangzeb defeated Shahaji and partitioned the sultanate between the Mughal Empire and the Sultanate of Bijapur', infobox 'Disestablished: October 1636'. Cliopatria's 1640-1652 'Ahmadnagar' shapes are the remnant that Cliopatria's Mughal Empire shape takes over only in 1653 (it holds 626 of the 627 cells of Ahmadnagar's 1579 shape).

correction.text: not an Ahmadnagar shape after October 1636: the remnant belongs to the Mughal Empire (and a share to Bijapur), 1648-1652

keyframe_review.note: As for 1640: the same remnant drawn as an Ahmadnagar shape for 1648-1652, twelve to sixteen years after the partition; Cliopatria's Mughal shape takes it from 1653.

region.text: Junnar and the Bahmani province around it

ledger.note: 1490: Malik Ahmad Nizam Shah I declares independence from the Bahmani Sultanate at Junnar and founds the Nizam Shahi line. 'On 28 May 1490, Ahmad declared independence and established the Nizam Shahi dynasty's rule'; he 'had been the Bahmani governor of Junnar'. The Bahmani page names his 1490 revolt with those of Yusuf Adil Shah and Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk.

1494: Ahmadnagar is founded and becomes the capital (infobox 'Ahmednagar (1494-1600)'; 'the new capital Ahmadnagar was founded in 1494'). Daulatabad fortress is secured in 1499 and ranks as a secondary capital to 1636.

region.text: two coastal cells on the Konkan edge (about 72.9-73.0 E, 19.1-19.3 N)

ledger.note: c. 1540: two cells of the northern Konkan coast pass to the Portuguese in Cliopatria's shapes. No page opened dates it; the Portuguese Empire dossier (am-06) should carry the matching gain.

region.text: a strip of about 12 cells on the Solapur-Naldurg side of the Bijapur frontier

ledger.note: c. 1547: Ahmadnagar's south-eastern frontier advances onto Bijapuri ground. The Adil Shahi page says Burhan Nizam Shah I 'besieged the Bijapuri city of Solapur four times, but did not retain it until a third invasion' and that Ali Adil Shah I's request for the return of Solapur and Kaliyani failed; no year is given, so 1547 is Cliopatria's.
c. 1552: the same strip reverts to Bijapur in Cliopatria's shapes; nothing on the pages opened dates the reversal (Kaliyani was returned in 1561, Solapur never).

1561: Hussain Nizam Shah I returns Kaliyani to Bijapur. 'Hussain sued for peace in 1561, submitting to Rama Raya and returning Kaliyani to Ali Adil Shah' (Adil Shahi page); in 1563 he besieged it again and abandoned the siege. Kaliyani lies outside Cliopatria's Ahmadnagar shapes (it is inside Bidar's).

1574: Murtaza Nizam Shah I annexes Berar, taking Ahmadnagar to its greatest extent. 'Murtaza Shah annexed Berar in 1574, bringing the sultanate to its territorial zenith' (Ahmadnagar page); 'proceeded to annex Berar into his own dominions of the Ahmadnagar Sultanate in 1574' (Berar page). Cliopatria dates the merged shape to 1579.

region.text: Berar and the country round Ahmadnagar, fought over from November 1595

ledger.note: November 1595: the Mughals invade Ahmadnagar. 'Ahmednagar was invaded by the Mughals in November 1595' (Chand Bibi page, regency of Bahadur Nizam Shah); in 1591 Akbar 'had asked all the four Deccan sultanies to acknowledge his supremacy'.

region.text: Berar and the country round Ahmadnagar

ledger.note: 23 February 1596: Chand Bibi makes peace with the Mughal prince Murad by ceding Berar; 'she decided to make peace by ceding Berar to Murad, who retreated'.
23 February 1596: Berar passes to the Mughals. 'On 23 February 1596, she decided to make peace by ceding Berar to Murad, who retreated.' Cliopatria gives Berar to the Mughals only in 1600.
1600: with Ahmadnagar lost, the Nizam Shahi court under Malik Ambar sits at Paranda (infobox 'Paranda (1600-1610)'); 'Malik Ambar backed Murtaza Nizam Shah II at Paranda' (Ahmadnagar page).

minus.text: the northern and eastern districts that Cliopatria moves to the Mughals in 1600

region.text: the 1600 loss other than Berar (about 73 cells) in Cliopatria's shapes

ledger.note: 18 August 1600: Ahmadnagar falls to the Mughals. 'Ahmednagar was captured by the Mughal forces of Daniyal and Mirza Yusuf Khan on 18 August 1600', after Chand Bibi 'was then killed by an enraged mob of her own troops'. Cliopatria's 1600 shape drops a further 73 cells to the Mughals besides Berar; the page names only the fort, so the region is the researcher's reading. Mughal capture of Ahmadnagar fort (18 August 1600) is a loss of the town itself, but the 237-cell 'rump' still contains it: the Nizam Shahi state lived on at Paranda, Junnar and Khirki and Malik Ambar later 'captured Ahmednagar Fort and town from the Mughals' (undated on the Malik Ambar page).

1610: the capital moves to Khirki, the new city of Malik Ambar, later Aurangabad (infobox 'Aurangabad (1610-1636)', 'Junnar (1610)'; Malik Ambar page: 'He founded/inhabited the city of Khirki in 1610').

region.text: the fortress of Daulatabad, secondary capital since 1499

ledger.note: 1633: Daulatabad falls to the Mughals. Fath Khan 'surrendered to the Mughals in the siege of Daulatabad' (Ahmadnagar page); the Nizam Shahi remnant continues under Shahaji and Murtaza Nizam Shah III to 1636.

region.text: Junnar and Mahuli, the last strongholds of the Nizam Shahi remnant

ledger.note: October 1636: Shahaji surrenders Mahuli and Junnar to the Mughals. 'In October 1636, Shahaji surrendered Mahuli and Junnar to the Mughals and returned to the Bijapur service' (Shahaji page); Shahaji's army had earlier captured Junnar and 'a large part of the northern Konkan region' (undated on the page).

region.text: the last of the Nizam Shahi remnant around Ahmadnagar, Junnar and Daulatabad

ledger.note: October 1636: the Nizam Shahi remnant is partitioned. 'In 1636 Aurangzeb defeated Shahaji and partitioned the sultanate between the Mughal Empire and the Sultanate of Bijapur' (the Adil Shahi page: 'In 1636, Bijapur signed a treaty agreeing to pay tribute to the Mughal emperor'). The page does not say where the line ran; the whole remnant is given to the Mughals here because Cliopatria's Mughal shape contains it from 1653 and no Bijapur shape gains it.
October 1636: the Ahmadnagar Sultanate ends, partitioned between the Mughal Empire and Bijapur (infobox 'Disestablished: October 1636'). Cliopatria keeps an 'Ahmadnagar' shape to 1652.

wars.name: Battle of Talikota
wars.outcome: Victory of the Deccan sultanates; 'Rama Raya was beheaded by Sultan Nizam Hussain himself' (Ahmadnagar page); no transfer of territory to Ahmadnagar is listed.
wars.note: Late January 1565 (23 January per the Talikota page); Berar did not take part according to the Talikota page.

wars.name: Mughal–Ahmadnagar conquest, 1595-1600
wars.outcome: Mughal victory: Berar ceded in February 1596; Ahmadnagar fort taken on 18 August 1600; Chand Bibi killed by her troops; the Nizam Shahi state survives as a remnant under Malik Ambar.
wars.note: Other pages mention Mughal operations of 1586 (Akbar's Mughals 'approached the capital, but were dispelled'; Ellichpur sacked) and the Battle of Rohankhed (1591); no territorial result.

wars.name: Mughal conquest of the Ahmadnagar remnant, 1633-1636
wars.outcome: Mughal victory: Daulatabad falls in 1633; in 1636 the sultanate is partitioned between the Mughal Empire and Bijapur and Shahaji enters Bijapur's service.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary line for Ahmadnagar; frontiers with Bijapur, Khandesh and Berar are Cliopatria's approximations. The October 1636 partition is dated but not delimited.

notes: Ahmadnagar (9 Cliopatria shapes, 1492-1652): the state ends in October 1636 so the 1640 and 1648 shapes are verdict wrong, and the 1619 shape holds only to 1636. Cliopatria's Mughal shape takes the remnant in 1653. The 1579 shape is Ahmadnagar plus Berar; the page dates the annexation to 1574 and the Mughal cession of Berar to 23 February 1596 (the Cliopatria Mughal shape has it from 1600); the Mughal dossier (sa-05) should carry a gain of Berar in February 1596 and of Ahmadnagar fort on 18 August 1600. No page gives an area for the sultanate. The 1547-1551 and 1552 strip changes at the Solapur border and the 1540 two-cell Konkan loss are not dated by any page opened. Malik Ambar's recovery of Ahmadnagar town (1600-1610s) is undated on the page; the rump keeps the town. The page gives no line for the 1636 partition between the Mughal Empire and Bijapur. Bijapur's Konkan/Janjira, the Habshi (Siddi) state of Janjira ('In 1618, the sultan [of Bijapur] lost the fortress of Janjira to the independent Habshi state of western India', Adil Shahi page) has no dossier: counterparts_needing_dossiers lists it. Place names Junnar and Mahuli are not in the gazetteer (listed in the report); Paranda is used only as a capital.
